summary: The root هشم (hshm) primarily means to break something, especially if it's dry or hollow, like a head. The verb هَشَّمَهُ (hashshamahu) implies breaking it severely or crushing it.
lane: 2 هَشَّمَهُ ذ , inf. n. تَهْشِيمٌ , He broke it [ much, or so crushed it ]; (TA;) namely, a dry thing, and anything hollow, such as the head, and the like. (TA in art. شدخ .)

headwords.def: هَشَّمَهُ, inf. n. تَهْشِيمٌ, He broke it [ much, or so crushed it ]; (TA;) namely, a dry thing, and anything hollow, such as the head, and the like. (TA in art. شدخ.)
تَهَشَّمَ It (a plant, or herbage,) became هَشِيم, i. e. dry, and broken in pieces.
هَشِيمٌ A plant that is dry, and breaks, or is broken, in pieces. (S, Msb, K.)
هَاشِمَةٌ A wound in the head which breaks the bone: see شَجَّةٌ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
